_comment: Bundled-tool sources. Two ways a tool lands on the drive: (1) STAGING - you download it once from the vendor page into a folder and pass -StagingDir; Build-Kit finds it by staging_glob, copies/extracts it, and logs its SHA-256. This is the robust path because most of these vendors don't publish stable URLs. (2) URL - for the few with a stable direct link, Build-Kit fetches automatically. Staging wins when both are available. See GET-TOOLS.md for exactly what to download and where each file goes.

tools.name: sysinternals-suite
tools._note: Stable URL, so this one auto-fetches even without staging. sdelete*.exe is removed post-extract (not whitelisted).

tools.name: microsoft-safety-scanner
tools._unpinned_reason: MSERT bundles its own malware signatures and expires ~10 days after download, so the binary legitimately differs on every build and a pinned hash would always be stale. Build-Kit logs the actual SHA-256 of the copy it ships.
tools._note: 64-bit MSERT. Auto-fetches via the fwlink; stage a msert.exe to override.

tools.name: adwcleaner
tools._note: Stage the single adwcleaner.exe from malwarebytes.com/adwcleaner.

tools.name: emsisoft-emergency-kit
tools._note: EEK self-extracts to a folder (default C:\EEK) containing Run\a2cmd.exe. Extract once, then place that whole EEK folder in staging named 'emsisoft' (a folder). GET-TOOLS.md has the steps.

tools.name: wiztree-portable
tools._note: The portable zip from diskanalyzer.com (has WizTree64.exe).

tools.name: smartmontools
tools._note: No official portable build. Install smartmontools once on the build machine (or 7-Zip-extract its installer) and place the resulting smartctl.exe (and any DLLs beside it) in staging. GET-TOOLS.md has the steps.

tools.name: speedtest-cli
tools._note: Ookla's URL is version-specific and changes; stage the current win64 zip from speedtest.net/apps/cli rather than pinning a URL that rots.

tools.name: nirsoft-bluescreenview
tools._note: Just BlueScreenView from nirsoft.net (the one CLAUDE.md references). Add other NirSoft zips to staging with matching globs if you extend the whitelist.

tools.name: snappy-driver-installer-origin
tools._note: From glenn.delahoy.com/snappy-driver-installer-origin. Stage the SDIO zip; add the NETWORK driverpack (drivers\DP_*LAN*/*WLAN*) into staging\SDIO too if you want offline NIC recovery (full packs are tens of GB - network-only is a few hundred MB).

tools.name: windows-debugging-tools-cdb
tools._note: cdb.exe + its DLLs from the Windows SDK 'Debugging Tools for Windows'. Install that SDK feature once, copy the x64 Debugging Tools folder, and place it in staging named 'windbg' (a folder). Optional / heaviest - skip for a first full build.

tools.name: win11debloat
tools._note: Source-code zip of a pinned release from github.com/Raphire/Win11Debloat/releases.

tools.name: oo-shutup10
tools._note: Single OOSU10.exe from oo-software.com/en/shutup10. Add your curated 'recommended.cfg' to staging too if you want a default profile shipped.
